title.narrative: Strengthening Rural Governance for the Right to Adequate Food Phase 2

description.narrative: Impact: Progressive governance for the right to food, guided by the principles of participation, transparency, accountability, non-discrimination, and rule of law, for improved food and nutrition security in rural communities.Outcome: Duty bearers in Ethiopia, progressively enact and implement inclusive legal frameworks, policies and programs that are conducive to the realization of the right to food and that promote accountability.

Strengthening Rural Governance for the Right to Adequate Food Phase 2 is a program that aims to promote good governance in and for rural areas. People living in rural areas, especially women, are suffering various intersecting forms of discrimination and their concerns are not sufficiently considered in decision-making processes on government policies, programs and budgets that affect their livelihoods.Current food system governance mechanisms tend to be siloed, often with limited participation, transparency, and accountability in decision-making processes. Through this program civil society collations and grassroot community and their networks will be strengthened and capacitated to become more effective advocacy actors especially connecting with Right to Food and rights-based approaches.

The project will directly reach a total of 14,979 people: (a)13,748 rights holders at the micro- and meso-levels in the intervention areas citizens directly reached through program activities, community members, particularly from marginalized groups .(b)179 members of Grassroots, CBO and CSO at the micro- and meso-levels, such as Women’s and Youth groups, Community Social Account-ability Committees (CSAC), Community Action Groups (CAG) will be empowered to raise their voice .(c)65 Leaders of these organizations and paralegals whose capacities are strengthened to facilitate social accountability processes and assist the community members on concerns related to their access to public programs, and potential human rights violations.(d)32 members of CSOs at the national level, who are supported to collaborate as coalition to increase their leverage in advocating for the Right to Food.(e)35 staff of the civil society partner organizations in this program, who will be strengthened in their role as convenors and facilitators of the coalitions and whose capacities will be further developed to influence national and international policy processes.(f)56 intermediaries such as journalists, academics, human rights institutions who will be involved as allies to raise awareness on the Right to Food, take up and disseminate advocacy demands.(g)365 duty bearers at the micro- and meso-levels in the intervention areas: government representatives, civil servants, local service providers who are sensitized about their role and obligations regarding the Right to Food and related entitlements.(h)500 duty bearers at the national level: government representatives, Members of Parliament, and civil servants, who are sensitized about their role and obligations regarding the Right to Food and lobbied take up the demands of the Right to Food coalitions in legislative and policy processes.Indirect target groups: 117,000 people Rights holders that benefit from more favorable legislature on meso-and macro-level
